docs/data-management.html.summary: Data management JLib Storage is intended for simple in-memory data management within an application or service. The storage classes maintain their values for the lifetime of the store instance. They do not provide persistence or database integration. For more advanced storage requirements, applications should use an appropriate persistent storage solution rather than relying on these in-memory components.

docs/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | JLib.Storage
docs/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started JLib Storage provides simple stores for working with collections of values. Integer storage The IntStore class can be used to add and retrieve integers and calculate their total. var store = new IntStore(); store.Add(10); store.Add(20); store.Add(30); var total = store.Sum(); IntStore uses functionality provided by JLib Tools to perform the calculation. String storage The StringStore class provides similar functionality for collections of strings. var store = new StringStore(); store.Add("First"); store.Add("Second"); var value = store.Get(0); See the API reference for the complete list of available types and members.
